title: Label-Free Hyperparameter Calibration for Parallel Context Encoding via KL Divergence Matching

contributions.purpose: Enable tuning of Adaptive Parallel Encoding (APE) hyperparameters when no ground-truth labels are available for calibration.
contributions.mechanism: Select APE's attention temperature and scaling factor by minimizing KL divergence between sequential-teacher and parallel-encoded next-token distributions, using only model-internal distributional signals.
contributions.evaluation: Method requires no labels; positioned as a label-free proxy (quantitative payoff reported in C2).
contributions.source_quote: We propose a label-free KL calibration method for APE hyperparameters that requires no ground-truth labels, using only model-internal distributional signals.

contributions.purpose: Show that distributional (KL) matching is more robust than small-sample label optimization for selecting APE hyperparameters.
contributions.mechanism: Compare KL-tuned APE against a label-tuned oracle on a downstream QA metric.
contributions.evaluation: KL-tuned APE reaches F1=48.09, outperforming the label-tuned oracle (F1=46.23) by +1.86 points on LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that KL-tuned APE (F1=48.09) outperforms label-tuned oracle (F1=46.23) by +1.86 points on LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA, showing that distributional matching is more robust than small-sample label optimization.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the KL landscape to understand which hyperparameter drives calibration behavior.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze sensitivity of temperature vs. scale and use multi-token KL averaging to break single-token degeneracy.
contributions.evaluation: Temperature dominates with 2.6x higher sensitivity than scale; multi-token KL averaging breaks the single-token degeneracy that always selects T=1.0.
contributions.domain: Hyperparameter landscape analysis for parallel encoding
contributions.source_quote: We analyze the KL landscape and find that temperature dominates with 2.6x higher sensitivity than scale, and that multi-token KL averaging breaks the single-token degeneracy that always selects T=1.0.

contributions.purpose: Provide practical deployment guidance on the reliability of KL-based hyperparameter selection.
contributions.mechanism: Bootstrap resampling stability analysis of temperature vs. scale selection with confidence intervals.
contributions.evaluation: Temperature selection is perfectly stable under bootstrap resampling (CI width=0.0) while scale selection is unstable (CI width=0.38).
contributions.source_quote: We provide stability analysis showing that temperature selection is perfectly stable under bootstrap resampling (CI width=0.0), while scale selection is unstable (CI width=0.38), offering practical guidance for deployment.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Adaptive Parallel Encoding (APE) (Yang et al., 2025) achieves state-of-the-art efficiency-quality trade-offs through two hyperparameters... APE's performance is sensitive to these hyperparameters, and current practice requires labeled validation data to tune them via grid search on downstream metrics such as F1.

APE (Yang et al. 2025) proposed adaptive parallel encoding with learnable temperature and scale parameters that modulate attention distributions... Our work addresses the practical challenge of calibrating APE's hyperparameters without labeled data.
Our work differs by using temperature not for calibration of output probabilities, but as a hyperparameter that controls the sharpness of attention distributions in parallel encoding.

In our setting, we use KL divergence as a label-free proxy for hyperparameter selection, measuring the distributional alignment between a sequential teacher and the parallel-encoded student across different hyperparameter configurations.
